sub_answers.sub_question: What disputes arose over representation of Bosnia's ethnic groups within the national team and football association?
sub_answers.text: Football in Bosnia became divided along ethnic lines during the war, with Bosnian Croats launching the Football Federation of Herzeg-Bosnia and its own league in 1993 and Bosnian Serbs organizing the First League of the Republika Srpska in 1993 [d55965203s4p0]. The Bosnian Football Association (N/FSBiH) competitions were effectively confined to territory under Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina institutions and were consequently Bosniak-majority, creating disputes over representation of the country's ethnic groups within national football structures [d55965203s4p0] [d63104390s1p0].

Which conflicts or controversies have emerged over ethnic representation (Bosniaks, Serbs, Croats) in Bosnia and Herzegovina’s national football team selection, management, and composition of the Football Association leadership?
sub_answers.text: Football in Bosnia and Herzegovina became divided along ethnic lines during the war, with Bosnian Croats forming the Football Federation of Herzeg-Bosnia and Bosnian Serbs organising the First League of the Republika Srpska, resulting in competitions segregated by ethnicity [d55965203s4p0]. This partition mirrored the wider ethnic conflict between Bosniaks, Croats and Serbs that followed the breakup of Yugoslavia and the Bosnian War [d63104390s1p0]. The N/FSBiH (Bosnian Football Association) competitions were suspended in many areas and only clubs under N/FSBiH auspices (largely Bosniak-majority areas) could initially participate, reflecting disputed representation and control over football governance during and after the war [d55965203s4p0].

sub_answers.text: Blaž Slišković had a prominent club career abroad, playing for Marseille in France and Pescara in Italy alongside notable spells at Velež Mostar and Hajduk Split domestically [d1108841s0p0]. Rusmir Cviko played outside Bosnia with Royal Antwerp in Belgium and finished his playing career at Al Wahda in the UAE after domestic spells including Željezničar [d52788023s1p0][d52788023s0p0]. During the war-era humanitarian fixtures, Refik Šabanadžović featured alongside many Bosnian-born players who had notable overseas careers after Yugoslavia, including Faruk Hadžibegić, Safet Sušić, Mehmed Baždarević, Meho Kodro and others [d8582465s6p0].
